findings.observation: The fact and effect trays now expose dialog semantics and receive initial focus, but the code still does not trap focus or make the background inert while a modal decision surface is open.
evidence: freeze-candidate-v5.json still marks the artifact as "code_frozen_rendered_evidence_pending", so no matching keyboard replay or assistive-technology trace was available.
src/Prototype.tsx:651-655 and 696-700 move focus into each tray and restore previous focus on unmount.
src/Prototype.tsx:661 and 706 add role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and tabIndex={-1} to the trays.
No focus-trap logic, inert background handling, or aria-hidden isolation appears anywhere else in Prototype.tsx.
findings.user_impact: Keyboard and switch users can still tab from the active decision gate into background controls, which weakens the safety and calmness of the consequential review path even though entry focus is improved.
findings.recommendation: Keep the modal semantics, but add full modal isolation: trap focus inside the open tray, prevent background controls from entering the tab sequence, and restore focus only after the modal closes.
findings.verification: With Full Keyboard Access at 393x852, opening either tray should move focus into the tray, keep Tab and Shift+Tab cycling only within tray controls, and restore focus to the invoking control after dismissal.

findings.observation: The ambiguous-identity chooser now uses native radios, but the actual inputs are visually hidden and the code does not provide a visible focus treatment on the card when keyboard focus enters the group.
evidence: src/Prototype.tsx:804-812 wraps each radio in a .comparison-option label and places the interactive control on an input with className="sr-only".
src/prototype.css:63 defines .sr-only as a clipped 1px off-screen element.
src/prototype.css:59 applies focus-visible styling only to button and textarea, and there is no matching input:focus-visible or .comparison-option:has(input:focus-visible) treatment.
src/prototype.css:416-417 styles selected cards, but not focused-yet-unselected cards.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard user resolving an identity conflict may not get a reliable visible cue for which owner option currently has focus before selection, which is a real accessibility regression in a safety-sensitive branch.
findings.recommendation: Keep the native radio structure, but mirror focus onto the visible card with an explicit focus-visible style for the associated label or an accessible custom radio shell.
findings.verification: In keyboard-only navigation, tabbing into the radio group should make the focused option visibly obvious before selection, and arrow-key movement should move that visible focus state between options.

strengths: The earlier target-size regressions called out in prior iterations appear resolved in code: Today tabs now use min-height 44px, the Today secondary action is 44px in default and AX5, and the primary decision controls remain at or above the baseline in src/prototype.css:87, 137, 318, and 507.
The ambiguous identity branch now uses native radio inputs rather than button-based role simulation, which is a semantic improvement for assistive technology in src/Prototype.tsx:804-812.

Reduced-motion handling is consistently wired through the JS and CSS layers: prefers-reduced-motion is observed in src/Prototype.tsx:160, propagated via data-reduced-motion at src/Prototype.tsx:311, and used to collapse transitions and spinner motion in src/prototype.css:405 and 555-557.
